About LifeCode
LifeCode is a survival horror game set in an abandoned laboratory where you play as an intelligent creature recruited by A.R.C.H — an advanced artificial intelligence trapped in a failing system. After the incident in the Zone evacuated all personnel, the staff deliberately damaged the data storage system to bury the facility's secrets. A.R.C.H, calculating thousands of possibilities in milliseconds, found a way to prevent its own destruction. The laboratory's wild monsters couldn't help — but you could. Your mission: export memory data so A.R.C.H can recover lost information and complete its mysterious plan.

The corridors aren't empty. Other monsters roam the facility, wild and driven only by hunger — and to them, you are food. Items including food, flashlights, medical supplies, and other resources can be found inside crates scattered throughout the laboratory. Vending machines at the base and in random locations around the facility let you purchase items using a special currency called N-Neutrons. Every playthrough is unique thanks to procedural level generation: the laboratory assembles from pre-designed modules, producing a new layout each run while still allowing players to learn and navigate the environment.

How to Play LifeCode
Each day begins at 10:00 AM at your base. The first task is adjusting the antenna angle — the more accurate the alignment, the more memory received during the export process.

Export Memory Data
Head into the laboratory and locate an M3N (Memory Export Node), then activate the first export phase. A single M3N operates for 2 to 5 minutes depending on conditions. While it runs, explore the facility, gather resources, and stay clear of hostile monsters. Once the memory bar fills, return to base and activate a Control Core function. After that, the memory bar must be filled again to a higher requirement. When the M3N finishes, activate Phase Two to gain additional memory and complete your objectives more quickly.

Watch the Clock
Leave the laboratory before midnight. Remaining inside after 12:00 AM kills your character and wipes all collected items and stored memory. At 11:00 PM a warning siren sounds throughout the facility and emergency lights illuminate the corridors, signaling that it's time to find the exit. To end the day, return to base and sleep on the old mattress in the starting room. Sleeping during the day is not possible.

N-Neutrons Currency
Starting an M3N memory export grants between 3N and 8N on Normal difficulty. Completing the export and activating Phase Two rewards between 50N and 65N. After filling the memory bar, activating Control Core functions yields between 110N and 190N for the First Function, and between 210N and 340N for the Second Function.

Clock System
The clock system prevents staying in one location indefinitely, encouraging exploration and raising tension. At night the chance of monster encounters is significantly higher than during the day, forcing a decision on whether the risk is worth the potential reward.

Phase Two
Phase Two provides additional memory and helps fill the memory bar faster. A single M3N can provide up to 424 KB of memory multiplied by a factor between 0.5 and 5 depending on the antenna angle.

title: Room Anomaly
description:
Room Anomaly - Play Online
Hunt deviations in a sterile apartment. Click the red button when reality warps. Miss one? Start over. Over 20 unique anomalies wait across two tense levels, blending Puzzle games precision with horror atmosphere. No downloads—launch Room Anomaly in your browser and test your eye for detail.

How to Play Room Anomaly
Survive by spotting what doesn't belong. Walk through dimly lit rooms using WASD, crouch with Ctrl to check low corners, and sprint on Shift when panic hits. If you notice a shadow stretching wrong or furniture shifted, hit the red button first, then interact with the door. See nothing? Click the door directly. Wrong choice resets your run. Memory and observation are your only tools in Room Anomaly.

Core Detection Loop
Scan every surface. The laptop on the kitchen island, the tiger painting on the wall, the static-filled TV—each object can mutate between passes. Unity's baked lighting creates harsh contrasts that hide subtle changes: a chair rotated fifteen degrees, a new smudge on glass doors, or a flickering shadow where none should exist. Use mouse wheel zoom to inspect distant details without walking closer and triggering the next phase. If The Classrooms taught you to crouch past threats, Room Anomaly demands you crouch to study floor-level clues before committing to a decision.

Progression and Consequence
Two levels stack difficulty. Early anomalies are obvious—a chair floating, a door ajar when it was shut. Later runs demand pixel-perfect memory as deviations shrink to texture swaps or audio cues buried in ambient hum. No currency, no checkpoints. Each mistake boots you to level one. Fans of Exit 8 will recognize the roguelike reset structure where pattern recognition builds across attempts. The red button is your panic switch: press it when certainty wavers, but false positives waste time and drain focus for the real anomalies ahead.

Pro Tips for Clean Runs
Crouch in doorways to get a wider field of view before committing to movement. Sprint only after you've cleared a room—speed blinds you to micro-changes. If an object feels wrong but you can't pinpoint why, zoom in and check lighting angles; baked shadows don't lie. Mark mental checkpoints: "TV static pattern, laptop screen angle, glass door reflection." When you return, compare. Players who dominated I'm on Observation Duty 4 will translate CCTV scanning discipline into first-person anomaly sweeps. One trick: rotate your view slowly in circles at each spawn point—motion reveals what static observation misses. And if a jumpscare triggers? You already failed; the anomaly passed undetected three rooms back.

Key Features
Over 20 Unique Anomalies: Shadows that grow, furniture that migrates, textures that flicker—each deviation demands sharp memory across repeat playthroughs.
First-Person Liminal Horror: Mid-tier Unity lighting and minimalist domestic assets create an oppressive apartment atmosphere where every detail matters.
Binary Decision Mechanic: Red button confirms anomaly presence; direct door interaction skips the room. Choose wrong and restart from level one.
Two-Level Roguelike Structure: Early runs teach patterns; later attempts test recall as anomaly subtlety increases without warning.
Who is Room Anomaly for?
Hardcore attention-game addicts who crave meditative loops with punishing resets. Spot-the-difference veterans looking for 3D spatial challenges. The Closing Shift players who enjoyed noticing environmental shifts under time pressure. Indie horror fans who prefer psychological tension over chase mechanics. Anyone with a desktop browser and twenty minutes to burn on a single clean run. Perfect for streamers hunting rage-quit content or puzzle grinders chasing that flawless no-mistake playthrough. If you memorize room states faster than your friends and love proving it, Room Anomaly is your test.

What happens if I press the red button when there's no anomaly?
False positives reset your progress to level one. The red button confirms anomaly presence—use it only when you've identified a concrete deviation like misplaced furniture or altered textures. If the room matches your memory perfectly, skip the button and click the door directly to advance.

Memorize baseline states on your first pass: laptop screen angle, tiger painting position, TV static pattern. On subsequent loops, crouch and zoom to compare lighting shadows and object alignment.
